src.q: Each tablet contains 50 mg of vildagliptin.
Each tablet contains 47.82 mg lactose (anhydrous).

items.t: Adults with type 2 diabetes, with diet and exercise: monotherapy when metformin is inappropriate (contraindicated or not tolerated); or with other diabetes medicines, including insulin, when these do not give adequate control.

src.q: as monotherapy in patients in whom metformin is inappropriate due to contraindications or intolerance
in combination with other medicinal products for the treatment of diabetes, including insulin, when these do not provide adequate glycaemic control

restrictions.note: No specialist-only, shared-care or brand-prescribing restriction found in the UK SmPC, MHRA or SPS pages checked.

items.t: 100 mg daily as 50 mg in the morning and 50 mg in the evening (monotherapy; with metformin; with a thiazolidinedione; with metformin plus a sulphonylurea; or with insulin with or without metformin). Doses above 100 mg are not recommended.

src.q: the recommended daily dose of vildagliptin is 100 mg, administered as one dose of 50 mg in the morning and one dose of 50 mg in the evening
Doses higher than 100 mg are not recommended.

items.t: Dual therapy with a sulphonylurea: 50 mg once daily in the morning (100 mg was no more effective). A lower sulphonylurea dose may be considered.

src.q: When used in dual combination with a sulphonylurea, the recommended dose of vildagliptin is 50 mg once daily administered in the morning.
When used in combination with a sulphonylurea, a lower dose of the sulphonylurea may be considered to reduce the risk of hypoglycaemia.

items.t: Moderate or severe renal impairment, or end-stage renal disease: 50 mg once daily (see Renal).

src.q: In patients with moderate or severe renal impairment or with end-stage renal disease (ESRD), the recommended dose of Galvus is 50 mg once daily

items.t: Elderly (65 years and over): no dose adjustment.

src.q: No dose adjustments are necessary in elderly patients

items.t: Missed dose: take as soon as remembered; do not take a double dose on the same day.

src.q: If a dose of Galvus is missed, it should be taken as soon as the patient remembers. A double dose should not be taken on the same day.

items.t: Not recommended under 18 years; safety and efficacy not established and no data.

src.q: Galvus is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (< 18 years).

items.t: Hypersensitivity to vildagliptin or any excipient.

src.q: Contraindications Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Not a substitute for insulin in insulin-requiring patients. Should not be used in type 1 diabetes or to treat diabetic ketoacidosis.

src.q: Galvus is not a substitute for insulin in insulin-requiring patients.
Galvus should not be used in patients with type 1 diabetes or for the treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis.

items.t: Hepatic impairment (including pre-treatment ALT or AST > 3 x ULN): should not be used. Rare hepatic dysfunction (including hepatitis) reported; check liver function before and during treatment (see Monitoring).

src.q: Galvus should not be used in patients with hepatic impairment, including patients with pre-treatment ALT or AST > 3x ULN
Rare cases of hepatic dysfunction (including hepatitis) have been reported.

items.t: Heart failure: no experience in NYHA class IV, so use is not recommended; experience in class III is limited.

src.q: There is no experience of vildagliptin use in clinical trials in patients with NYHA functional class IV and therefore use is not recommended in these patients.
Clinical experience in patients with NYHA functional class III treated with vildagliptin is still limited and results are inconclusive

items.t: End-stage renal disease on haemodialysis: limited experience; use with caution.

src.q: There is limited experience in patients with ESRD on haemodialysis. Therefore Galvus should be used with caution in these patients

items.t: Acute pancreatitis: inform patients of the symptoms. If suspected, stop vildagliptin; do not restart if confirmed. Caution with a history of acute pancreatitis.

src.q: If pancreatitis is suspected, vildagliptin should be discontinued; if acute pancreatitis is confirmed, vildagliptin should not be restarted.
Caution should be exercised in patients with a history of acute pancreatitis.

items.t: Skin: blistering and exfoliative skin lesions reported after marketing; monitor for skin disorders such as blistering or ulceration.

src.q: monitoring for skin disorders, such as blistering or ulceration, is recommended

items.t: Hypoglycaemia with a sulphonylurea: a lower sulphonylurea dose may be considered.

src.q: Patients receiving vildagliptin in combination with a sulphonylurea may be at risk for hypoglycaemia.

items.t: Contains lactose: patients with rare hereditary galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: Low interaction potential: not a CYP450 substrate, inhibitor or inducer.

src.q: Vildagliptin has a low potential for interactions with co-administered medicinal products.

items.t: Sulphonylureas: hypoglycaemia risk; a lower sulphonylurea dose may be considered (vildagliptin 50 mg once daily in dual therapy).

src.q: Therefore, a lower dose of sulphonylurea may be considered to reduce the risk of hypoglycaemia.

items.t: ACE inhibitors: there may be an increased risk of angioedema (cases were mostly mild and resolved on continued vildagliptin).

src.q: There may be an increased risk of angioedema in patients concomitantly taking ACE-inhibitors.
The majority of events were mild in severity and resolved with ongoing vildagliptin treatment.

items.t: Thiazides, corticosteroids, thyroid products and sympathomimetics may reduce the glucose-lowering effect.

src.q: the hypoglycaemic effect of vildagliptin may be reduced by certain active substances, including thiazides, corticosteroids, thyroid products and sympathomimetics

items.t: No clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interaction with metformin, pioglitazone, glibenclamide, digoxin, warfarin, amlodipine, ramipril, valsartan or simvastatin.

src.q: Combination with pioglitazone, metformin and glyburide Results from studies conducted with these oral antidiabetics have shown no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interactions.
Digoxin (Pgp substrate), warfarin (CYP2C9 substrate) Clinical studies performed with healthy subjects have shown no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interactions.
In these studies, no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interactions were observed after co-administration with vildagliptin.

items.t: Mild renal impairment (CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min): no dose adjustment.

src.q: No dose adjustment is required in patients with mild renal impairment (creatinine clearance ≥ 50 ml/min).

items.t: Moderate or severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease (the SmPC defines mild as CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min, so this means CrCl < 50 mL/min): 50 mg once daily.

src.q: In patients with moderate or severe renal impairment or with end-stage renal disease (ESRD), the recommended dose of Galvus is 50 mg once daily

items.t: End-stage renal disease on haemodialysis: limited experience; use with caution.

src.q: Therefore Galvus should be used with caution in these patients

items.t: Should not be used in hepatic impairment, including pre-treatment ALT or AST > 3 x ULN.

src.q: Galvus should not be used in patients with hepatic impairment, including patients with pre-treatment alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) > 3x the upper limit of normal (ULN)

items.t: SmPC: no adequate human data; animal reproductive toxicity at high doses. Should not be used in pregnancy.

src.q: There are no adequate data from the use of vildagliptin in pregnant women.
Due to lack of human data, Galvus should not be used during pregnancy.

items.t: BUMPS: type 2 diabetes in pregnancy should be treated with metformin, with insulin if needed; other antidiabetic medicines (including DPP-4 inhibitors) are avoided as a precaution. In an unplanned pregnancy, continue current treatment until reviewed promptly.

src.q: Type 2 diabetes during pregnancy should be treated with metformin, as well as insulin if required. Other antidiabetic drugs should not be used.
you should carry on with the drug you are taking until your appointment, as uncontrolled diabetes is risky for you and your baby

items.t: SmPC: unknown if excreted in human milk (excreted in animal milk). Should not be used during breastfeeding.

src.q: It is unknown whether vildagliptin is excreted in human milk.
Galvus should not be used during breast-feeding.

items.t: SPS: insulin or metformin are the preferred choices; there is limited or no published information on other antidiabetic medicines in breastfeeding.

src.q: Insulin or metformin are the preferred choices during breastfeeding.
limited or no published information on the use of other antidiabetic (blood-glucose lowering) medicines during breastfeeding

items.t: Fertility: no human studies.

src.q: No studies on the effect on human fertility have been conducted for Galvus

items.t: Very common: nasopharyngitis. Common: upper respiratory tract infection, dizziness, headache, tremor, blurred vision, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal pain, gastro-oesophageal reflux, sweating, rash, itching, dermatitis, joint and muscle pain, weakness, peripheral oedema.

items.t: Uncommon: hypoglycaemia (more with a sulphonylurea plus metformin, or with insulin), abnormal liver function tests.

src.q: Hypoglycaemia Uncommon
Abnormal liver function tests Uncommon

items.t: Hepatic dysfunction including hepatitis (rare): stop if jaundice or signs of liver dysfunction; do not restart after liver tests return to normal.

src.q: Patients who develop jaundice or other signs suggestive of liver dysfunction should discontinue Galvus.
Following withdrawal of treatment with Galvus and LFT normalisation, treatment with Galvus should not be reinitiated.

items.t: Acute pancreatitis (rare): stop if suspected; do not restart if confirmed.

src.q: Pancreatitis Rare
if pancreatitis is suspected, the DPP-4 inhibitor and other potentially suspect medicines should be discontinued

items.t: Exfoliative and bullous skin lesions including bullous pemphigoid; cutaneous vasculitis; angioedema (rare, more often with ACE inhibitors).

src.q: Exfoliative and bullous skin lesions, including bullous pemphigoid Not known*
Rare cases of angioedema have been reported on vildagliptin at a similar rate to controls.

items.t: Liver function tests before starting.

src.q: Liver function tests should be performed prior to the initiation of treatment with Galvus in order to know the patient's baseline value.

items.t: Liver function every 3 months in the first year, then periodically. If transaminases rise, repeat to confirm and follow frequently until normal.

src.q: Liver function should be monitored during treatment with Galvus at three-month intervals during the first year and periodically thereafter.
Patients who develop increased transaminase levels should be monitored with a second liver function evaluation to confirm the finding

items.t: Skin: monitor for blistering or ulceration.

src.q: monitoring for skin disorders, such as blistering or ulceration, is recommended

items.t: Withdrawal recommended if AST or ALT ≥ 3 x ULN persists; stop if jaundice or liver dysfunction (do not restart); stop if pancreatitis is suspected.

src.q: Should an increase in AST or ALT of 3x ULN or greater persist, withdrawal of Galvus therapy is recommended.
Patients who develop jaundice or other signs suggestive of liver dysfunction should discontinue Galvus.

items.t: Oral; with or without a meal.

src.q: Galvus can be administered with or without a meal

items.t: Swallowing difficulty (SPS, off-label): can be crushed and mixed with water or given with soft food.

src.q: Vildagliptin tablets Can be crushed and mixed with water or given with soft food.

items.t: Seek medical help for persistent, severe abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis), or for yellow skin or eyes (possible liver problem).

src.q: persistent, severe abdominal pain (sometimes radiating to the back)
Patients who develop jaundice or other signs suggestive of liver dysfunction should discontinue Galvus.

items.t: If dizzy, avoid driving or using machines.

src.q: Patients who experience dizziness as an adverse reaction should avoid driving vehicles or using machines.

items.t: Attend liver blood tests as arranged.

src.q: Liver function should be monitored during treatment with Galvus at three-month intervals during the first year and periodically thereafter.
